# US Grid Demand Dashboard

> A free tool from Kardashev Labs showing real-time and forecast US electricity demand across 15 balancing authorities, covering approximately 95% of the continental United States (CONUS).

The dashboard visualizes live and historical electricity demand (load) reported by US balancing authorities and ISOs, sourced from the EIA Open Data API via the kardashev-data platform. It is intended for anyone tracking grid load patterns: analysts, researchers, energy traders, and engineers.

## What the data means

- **Demand / load**: The amount of electricity (megawatts) being consumed on a balancing authority's system at a given hour.
- **Balancing authority**: A regional entity responsible for matching electricity supply and demand in real time (e.g., CAISO, ERCOT, PJM, MISO).
- **Forecast demand**: Day-ahead or short-term load forecasts published by the balancing authority or EIA, shown alongside actuals for comparison.
- **CONUS coverage**: The dashboard's 15 tracked balancing authorities collectively represent roughly 95% of continental US electricity demand.

## Coverage

15 US balancing authorities including CAISO, ERCOT, PJM, MISO, SPP, NYISO, ISO-NE, and others, refreshed on an hourly cadence from EIA data.

## Key facts

- Free and open source
- Source code: https://github.com/kardashev-lab
- Part of Kardashev Labs: https://kardashevlabs.org
- Data source: EIA Open Data API (https://www.eia.gov/opendata/), served via kardashev-data (https://data.kardashevlabs.org)
- Contact: ashutosh@kardashevlabs.org

## Architecture note

This dashboard is a client-rendered single-page app (Vite + React) with no server-side rendering, so page content is not visible to crawlers that do not execute JavaScript. Structured data (JSON-LD) is embedded statically in index.html to describe the tool, but live demand numbers are only visible in-browser.

## About Kardashev Labs

Kardashev Labs builds free, open-source tools for US energy grid intelligence, accelerating humanity toward Kardashev Type I by making grid data universally accessible.
